summary: Backend trial endpoints (/api/subscription/status, /api/subscription/info, /api/subscription/reset-to-trial) all correctly recognize trial for user_id=default and new users (5/5 pytest passing). Frontend /subscription page correctly displays the trial banner (data-testid='trial-active-banner' = 'Free trial active — full access') and no plan card is marked 'Current plan'. However, /training and /sessions tabs are STILL blocked with a paywall UI on trial due to a subscription middleware bug (see RCA).

critical.issue: Middleware only reads user_id from ?user_id= query param, falling back to client IP. It does NOT read the 'X-User-Id' header that the frontend actually sends (TrainingPlan.jsx, Progress.jsx, WorkoutDetail all use headers: { 'X-User-Id': USER_ID }). Result: requests are attributed to an IP-based synthetic user which lands on status='free' -> 403 subscription_required on /api/workouts, /api/training/plan, /api/training/full-cycle, /api/training/race-predictions. The trial that the Subscriptions page shows is therefore not honored on Training/Sessions pages.

integration_issues.flow: Training tab access while on 30-day trial
integration_issues.issue: /training returns Paywall-like UI ('Activate your running coach') because underlying /api/training/plan and /api/training/full-cycle return HTTP 403 subscription_required. Root cause is the backend middleware bug above, not the frontend isFree check (SubscriptionContext correctly reports trial).
/api/workouts returns 403 for the same reason (X-User-Id header ignored by middleware). No session links render on /sessions; workout detail cannot be exercised end-to-end.

action_items: Fix get_user_id_from_request in /app/backend/server.py (line 244) to ALSO read the X-User-Id header before falling back to X-Forwarded-For / client IP, e.g.: `user_id = request.query_params.get('user_id') or request.headers.get('X-User-Id')`. Without this, the subscription middleware wrongly classifies frontend requests as anonymous IP-based users and returns 403 even when the real user (default) has an active trial.

After the fix, re-verify: GET /api/workouts with header X-User-Id: default returns 200, /training page renders the 18-week plan, /sessions page lists workouts, clicking a session opens /workout/:id without showing 'Workout not found'.

Confirmed working already: /subscription page (trial banner + Free not marked as current), /progress page (RunIndex 352/1000 chart renders), backend subscription/status + subscription/info + reset-to-trial for both existing (default) and brand-new (qa_trial_check_001) user IDs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:244 get_user_id_from_request lacks parity with auth_user (server.py:262-275) which correctly checks X-User-Id header. The two helpers must agree, otherwise the middleware gate diverges from the endpoint's own user resolution.

The subscription middleware falls back to client IP as user_id. For a public preview URL behind a proxy, this collapses many callers onto the same synthetic user; whatever status is stored there (often 'free' after a prior trial expired) blocks everyone. Consider requiring an explicit user identifier or defaulting to 'default' rather than IP.
server.py is 5611 lines; splitting subscription middleware, auth helpers and route groups into modules would help maintainability.

rca of the issue: RCA: The frontend TrainingPlan.jsx, Progress.jsx and WorkoutDetail send user identity exclusively via `headers: { 'X-User-Id': USER_ID }` (USER_ID='default'). The backend subscription_middleware(server.py:329) calls get_user_id_from_request(server.py:244) which only inspects `request.query_params.get('user_id')` and then falls back to `X-Forwarded-For` / `request.client.host`. The X-User-Id header is silently ignored, so the middleware looks up a subscription for an IP-based synthetic user_id whose stored status is 'free' (either never provisioned or a prior expired trial). Middleware then returns 403 subscription_required, and the Training page renders its 'Activate your running coach' fallback. Repro: `curl -H 'X-User-Id: default' https://<base>/api/workouts` -> 403 with `{status:'free'}`; `curl 'https://<base>/api/workouts?user_id=default'` -> 200 with the workouts list. Mitigation: In get_user_id_from_request, add `or request.headers.get('X-User-Id')` before the IP fallback; this mirrors auth_user() and immediately unblocks Training/Sessions on trial without touching any business logic.
